titulo: Who sees the tool: same origin, exposedTo, iframes and Permissions-Policy
lead: By default, only the page itself and same-origin pages can see the tool. An iframe from another origin shows up to the top page only with three consents, and a header turns everything off. In this lesson you measure the seven cases in Chromium and put Permissions-Policy: tools=() on the pages that do not need WebMCP.
objetivo: measure who sees each tool (same origin, iframe, exposedTo, fromOrigins) and turn WebMCP off with Permissions-Policy where it should not exist.

aprende.t: Origin = scheme + host + port, and the spec's exposure default
The iframe's three consents: allow="tools", exposedTo and fromOrigins
Permissions-Policy: tools=() turns the API off before any script runs
Seven cases measured in Chromium 156 against the spec of October 16, 2026

hero_alt: Two overlapping browser windows on a dark monitor, one inside the other, with a connector between them.

secoes.sub: Click each one. Top = the main page; iframe = a page from another origin inside it.

nos.detalhe: Permissions-Policy: tools=() in the server response leaves the page and all its iframes without the API: registerTool and getTools fail with NotAllowedError. The default for the tools feature is 'self' (§4.4).
<iframe allow="tools">: the top page lets the iframe from another origin use the API. Without it, the iframe's registerTool fails with NotAllowedError.
registerTool(def, { exposedTo: ['https://topo.exemplo'] }): the iframe agrees to show the tool to that origin. Trusted origins only (https or local); a public http:// gives SecurityError.
getTools({ fromOrigins: ['https://iframe.exemplo'] }): the top page asks to see that origin. Only with all three (allow, exposedTo and fromOrigins) does the top page see the iframe's tool.

secoes.legenda: Measured in Chromium 156.0.8078.4 with the WebMCP test flag (experimental as of October 19, 2026). The spec's origin boundaries section (§6.3.4) is still just a to-do note.

secoes.sub: The top page runs on 127.0.0.1 on one port, and the iframe runs on 127.0.0.1 on another port. Same machine, different port: different origin.

blocos.conteudo:
<!doctype html>
<!-- filho.html — the page inside the iframe (it can be from another origin). Tries to register a tool.
     Parameter (lab only): ?exposto=<origin>  becomes  registerTool(..., { exposedTo: [<origin>] }) -->
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>iframe</title>
<script>
  (async () => {
    const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
    const mc = document.modelContext;
    let estado = 'sem WebMCP';
    if (mc) {
      try {
        const opcoes = q.get('exposto') ? { exposedTo: [q.get('exposto')] } : {};
        await mc.registerTool({ name: 'ferramenta_iframe', description: 'Ferramenta do iframe.',
          inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: {} }, execute: async () => ({ ok: true }) }, opcoes);
        estado = 'registrou';
      } catch (e) { estado = 'recusou: ' + e.name; }
    }
    parent.postMessage({ iframe: estado }, '*');
  })();
</script>

abas.html:
== Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright) · modo: nativo
confere 0 · iframe da MESMA origem, sem nada → vê: mesma origem é o padrão
confere A · iframe de outra origem, sem allow="tools" → iframe recusado (NotAllowedError)
confere B · allow="tools", sem exposedTo → topo não vê
confere C · allow + exposedTo:[topo], topo sem fromOrigins → topo não vê
confere D · allow + exposedTo:[topo] + fromOrigins:[iframe] → topo VÊ a ferramenta do iframe
confere E · topo com Permissions-Policy: tools=() → topo e iframe recusados
confere F · exposedTo com origem http:// pública → iframe recusado (SecurityError)
7/7 casos conferem com a spec
saída: 0

Only in case D does the top page see the iframe's tool, and the result carries its origin (ferramenta_iframe@http://127.0.0.1:…). The agent can use that field to avoid mixing up whose tool it is.

texto: If the tool belongs only to your page, don't use exposedTo. Same origin already sees it, and no other origin needs to.
Chat widget, ad, video: an iframe from another origin without allow="tools". That way it can't register any tool in your document.
Login, payment, privacy: send Permissions-Policy: tools=(). The spec (§6.4.1) says this protects even against injected script or a compromised dependency, because it applies before any script runs.
Seeing the tool doesn't mean being able to do everything. The backend still checks who the person is and what they can do, just like with the button.

secoes.sub: The kit's server sends tools=() on the privacy page and nothing on the main page. Alongside it, the same header on three common servers.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-seguranca-v72/kit
node scripts/servir.mjs & P=$!
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8742/; do sleep 0.3; done
curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8742/privacidade.html | grep -i '^permissions-policy'
curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8742/ | grep -ci '^permissions-policy'
kill $P; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
página em http://127.0.0.1:8742/
Permissions-Policy: tools=()
0
saída: 0

The privacy page sends tools=(); the main page sends 0 Permissions-Policy headers (it needs the API).

exercicios.pronto: 7/7 casos conferem com a spec and saída: 0.
Permissions-Policy: tools=() on the privacy page and 0 on the main page.

exercicios.texto: Pick the pages on your site that don't register a tool (login, payment, privacy), set the header on your server, and check each one with curl -sI [page address] | grep -i permissions-policy.
exercicios.pronto: Each page on the list responds with permissions-policy: tools=().

perguntas.p: An iframe from another origin registered a tool with exposedTo pointing at the top page, but the top page can't see it. What's missing?
opcoes: The top page calling getTools with fromOrigins pointing at the iframe
The iframe changing exposedTo to http:// to be more open
A Permissions-Policy: tools=() header on the top page
Registering the tool twice, once in each document
perguntas.explica: Measured (case C × D): exposedTo is the iframe's consent; fromOrigins is the top page's request. You need both, plus allow="tools".

perguntas.p: Which page should send Permissions-Policy: tools=()?
opcoes: The main page, which registers the site's tools
Every page that has a video iframe from the site itself
Only pages served over http:// without a certificate
The payment page, which doesn't register a tool
perguntas.explica: tools=() turns the API off in the document and in its iframes. Use it where WebMCP isn't intended: it protects even against injected script (§6.4.1).

opcoes: The top page now sees the tool without needing fromOrigins
registerTool rejects with SecurityError: untrusted origin
The tool becomes visible to every origin in the world, no exceptions
Nothing changes: the list is ignored outside Chrome Canary
perguntas.explica: The spec requires a potentially trustworthy origin in the list. Measured in Chromium 156: "Only secure origins are allowed in the exposedTo list".

perguntas.p: The tool shows up for the top page. Does that authorize any action it takes?
opcoes: Yes: if the browser exposed it, the backend can trust the call
Yes, as long as the page uses https on every route
No: the backend checks the person and the permission, just like for a button
No, because the browser turns the tool off after one call
perguntas.explica: Exposure decides who sees it. Authorization stays on the server, just like the person's click.

itens.texto: Same origin sees it; another origin sees nothing.
Only with allow="tools", exposedTo and fromOrigins together.
tools=() on pages that don't need the API.
